messages:
olivia: Anyone else hit a stream cancel when auth refresh happens mid-generation? I hit it on the sample app during onboarding tests.
kevin: Yep saw something similar yesterday. Can you paste a minimal repro?
olivia: Repro steps: start generator stream on a long prompt, then rotate credentials (we simulate refresh). The stream returns an error 'stream closed by peer' and the iterator stops. Not seeing ctx cancel on our side.
kevin: Hmm. Is the sample app creating a new HTTP client/transport on token refresh? If the underlying connection/handshake changes the server can close the stream.
sam: Quick workaround: reuse the same transport and swap tokens via a RoundTripper that reads token from func at request time. That avoids connection resets.
olivia: We do recreate the client to attach new token, since our KMS hook returns full creds object. That explains it. But UX-wise this is nasty for users following the sample.
kevin: For the Go SDK generator stream we generally expect callers to pass a context that governs lifecycle. Example pattern:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(req.Context())
defer cancel()
iter := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
for iter.Next() {
    // handle tokens
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
    // handle error
}
```
If the SDK is reopening the connection under the hood during auth handshake, it should preserve stream semantics or return a clear retryable error.
olivia: The problem is subtle: when token rotate triggers, we saw connection-level reset but the iterator returned a non-actionable error (io.EOF / stream closed) so apps assume completion.
kevin: File a small repro and I'll add a regression test. Can you capture logs with DEBUG for the runtime handshake? Also paste the exact error string.
olivia: Error: "rpc error: code = Canceled desc = stream terminated by peer" — attaching logs in a follow-up thread.
devex-bot: new test-created: devex/stream-auth-rotation/repro-186543 (link) :white_check_mark:
sam: Proposal: update sample app to show two patterns—1) reuse RoundTripper with token-provider func, 2) if you must recreate client, explicitly cancel and restart the generator iteration and surface intent to user.
kevin: Agreed. Also consider improving Go SDK ergonomics: provide a helper StreamWithAuthRefresh(ctx, req, opts...) that handles in-flight auth swap gracefully (i.e., transparently retries or signals ErrAuthRotate).
olivia: That helper would cut onboarding friction a lot. Right now new users copy sample code and hit this race.
sam: Small patch idea: detect net/http connection reset vs user cancel and return a typed error constants (ErrStreamAuthRotate, ErrStreamConnReset) so apps can decide to retry.
kevin: I'll sketch the error types. If we add docs and a small sample showing the RoundTripper approach, that should reduce support tickets.
olivia: Filing a docs PR after I attach logs. Thanks — will follow up with repro link. :thumbsup:
